thumbnail_brief: One huge olive-green anaconda coil filling two thirds of the frame at feed size, its head low in dark water with two eye bumps, tiny red-capped Doug standing on the coil as if it were a log, with the words NOT A LOG, so the title gives the snake's weight and its missing venom and the thumbnail gives the ambush (no ANACONDA, VENOM, KILL or KG on the image; no blood, no body-shaped lump, no big cute snake eyes, no capybara).
description:
A wild green anaconda weighed 97.5 kg, more than the average man, and it has no venom at all. Doug follows one anaconda hunt from start to finish, from two bumps on the water to the bite, the squeeze that (in studies on its cousin, the boa) stops the blood before the breath, the swallow, and the 30-foot snake nobody ever claimed a prize for.

Which animal should Doug never be allowed to measure? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe so you don't miss Doug's next bad decision.
